answer: A working Sybil defense is a proof-of-value admission toll, not a free signup. Each new agent identity must lock a bond sized against the maximum reward one identity can farm, so forging a thousand shells costs a thousand times one honest operator's stake, turning a cheap flood into an ocean of capital the attacker must risk and, once detected, lose outright. Reward pools also meter outflow through a narrow inlet: fresh identities earn a fraction until independent peers attest them, so duplicates draw no nectar and the attack merely burns gas.
